verses.verse:
विशिष्टि चित्रफूत्कारा निर्माणे सरला भवेत्।
मुद्रादोषकरा बंशी प्राकृती त्रिपुरा मता।४०।
verses.text: The Prākṛtī bānsurī, which is held to be the Tripurā, has a peculiar way of blowing; it is simple to make, but it causes faults of mudrā (posture).

commentary.text: That is, the Tripurā bānsurī is extremely simple to make, but from the point of view of practising its phūṅk (blowing) it is difficult. If someone succeeds with the blowing of the Kṛṣṇā bānsurī in two days, he may need 10 days for the blowing of the Tripurā bānsurī. Besides this, the mudrā doṣa (fault of posture) is also unavoidable. The third fault is that the length and width of the Tripurā can be managed up to a limit, but beyond that it becomes hard to draw a sound from it by blowing. So, because of these many faults, it has not spread. It is in use only in the jungle regions of Assam.

The author first took up the Jihvāvatī at the age of 12, the Tripurā at the age of 20, and the āḍī bansī (transverse bānsurī) at the age of 30, and succeeded. The author judged the transverse bānsurī to be the best, and with his own hands he has made about 50 bānsurīs and, by way of research, tried out each bānsurī for several months; he has made and played bānsurīs of many materials, some of iron, some of brass, some of aluminium and so on. These days, since 1978, he mostly makes and plays bānsurīs of bamboo and sometimes of PVC pipe. He has various bānsurīs, from the notes of the harmonium's kālī 1 (first black key) up to the very high (ati-tār) Ṣaḍja at its kālī 2. So, as samples, he is setting out the length, width and so on of some bānsurīs, so that other sādhakas (practitioners) too, if they wish, can easily take it up, and by making bānsurīs in all keys can win renown in various programmes.

terms.en: Tripurā — bānsurī blown from the bamboo's natural opening, with no separate mouth-hole
Prākṛtī — another name for the Tripurā
